text: A lien gets recorded against a New York building. And the token that represents shares in that building? It has no idea. This is Liensight.

Real estate is being tokenized. Shares in a single building can trade on-chain, around the clock. But the law doesn't pause. A tax lien, a federal lien, a judgment: any of them can land on that property. Today, someone has to remember to check the county record. The chain never looks. And the shares keep moving.

Why Chainlink C.R.E.? A lien lives in a government database, and a smart contract can't read one. C.R.E. lets a decentralized network of nodes fetch that A.P.I., agree on the answer, and write it on-chain, with no single server to trust. Our workflow is four steps: a cron trigger, an H.T.T.P. capability, consensus, and an E.V.M. write.

Every ten minutes, each node independently queries two New York A.C.R.I.S. datasets for the building. The nodes must return the identical document set, or nothing is written, and incomplete data fails closed. The report is signed and delivered through the Chainlink forwarder. The token checks the workflow owner and the property, then restricts transfers and cites the lien. Only the issuer can clear it.

Now, the live demo. This is a real lot in the Bronx, read live from A.C.R.I.S. Fourteen documents on record, and one of them is a lien of common charges, recorded on September thirtieth. A building in Manhattan: nothing adverse, so transfers would stay open.
Now the real workflow, run with the C.R.E. C.L.I. It compiles our TypeScript to WebAssembly, then the cron trigger fires.
The nodes read A.C.R.I.S., flag the lien, and write a signed report to the token on Sepolia.
There's the transaction on the block explorer: success, delivered by the Chainlink forwarder. And on the token itself, restricted is true. Even the issuer can't move shares now.
And on the token's event log: the report call, and a Restricted event carrying the same document-set hash the nodes agreed on. Anyone can verify it.

Why this fits this hackathon. It's a real-world-asset project grounded in official county land records. It's a working Chainlink C.R.E. workflow that connects a blockchain to an external A.P.I., simulated and broadcast on Sepolia. Thirty-five tests pass, and a security review found and fixed one critical and five important issues before deployment.

And it's honest about its limits. Testnet only. The records lag real events by days. And lis pendens aren't in A.C.R.I.S., so they're out of scope. Next: a deployed workflow, the production forwarder, and a second data source.
Liensight. The token finds out when the building does.
